This test checks that neither importing a multi-file package from a build-tagged
test file (producing an ITV "example.com/tools/tool [command-line-arguments.test]")
nor having a multi-file package whose import path contains "command-line-arguments"
triggers a bug report asserting unexpected files in a command-line-arguments
package (golang/go#64557, and the single-file case in golang/go#66109).

Depends on go1.22+ go list errors.

-- flags --
-min_go_command=go1.22

-- go.mod --
module example.com/tools

go 1.22

-- tools_test.go --
//go:build tools

package tools //@diag("tools", re"No packages found")

import (
	_ "example.com/tools/tool"
)

-- tool/tool.go --
package main

func main() {
	Helper() //@def("Helper", Helper)
}

-- tool/other.go --
package main

func Helper() { //@loc(Helper, "Helper")
}

-- command-line-arguments/a.go --
package cli

func A() {
	B() //@def("B", B)
}

-- command-line-arguments/b.go --
package cli

func B() { //@loc(B, "B")
}
